rv.q: But there’s no escaping that the storyline piles one cliché on another, and the way the show addresses mental health issues is earnest but trite.
But in Memon’s liquid-gold singing voice, the emotional beats almost pierce your skin.
But it’s Memon’s performance, oozing warmth and charisma, that makes this exceptionally crafted piece of gig theatre soar.
Manic Street Creature is a calling card for Memon’s considerable array of talents.
Memon triumphs in articulating a tale of true despair and hope.
She is vivid, she is real, and she is alive in an astounding piece of musical theatre.
But while Manic Street Creature doesn’t always work as a piece of theatre, it absolutely does as a compelling, emotionally resonant showcase of Memon’s skill as both a performer and storyteller.

The material possesses moments of gentle comedy and touching pathos, most of all it has an inherent humanity and subtly asks us to consider the stark realities of mental health issues from different angles and perspectives.
The songs are wonderful and tell the story so clearly; it just felt like a few more songs instead of the spoken word towards the end could have really rocked the piece.
